newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Durables, Chicago PMI in focus Nov 25 wk.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Durables, Chicago PMI in focus Nov 25 wk.

text.p: Reports set for late next week will suggest slower growth in U.S. factory employment and manufacturing, according to a Reuters poll on Friday.

Many of the 22 economists surveyed said Wednesday's report on October durable goods orders and Friday's release of the November index of the Purchasing Management Association of Chicago (Chicago PMI) would be next week's key data.
"Durables are a forward-looking factor and Chicago would be a forward-looking factor," said Astrid Adolfson, first vice president and senior economist at MCM MoneyWatch Inc.
On average, experts estimated a 2.0 percent dip in durables last month after a 4.9 percent jump in September.
"The rise was almost all aircraft orders, and that's going to back off," said John Park, an economist at Sanwa Securities USA Co.
A drop in durables would indicate at least a temporary slowdown in demand for big-ticket items. "That means manufacturing jobs should still be weak," said Adolfson.
Chicago PMI, an assessment of Chicago-area manufacturing conditions, slipped to 55.1 this month from 56.9 in October, according to the average estimate of survey respondents.

"The Chicago index has been running stronger than some of the other manufacturing indicators, so I think (it will) fall back more in line with the pattern that we're seeing in other regional indicators," said John Ryding, senior economist at Bear Stearns & Co Inc.
Growth in manufacturing appears to have slowed in October and stabilized in November, Ryding said, adding that that was "a very preliminary take."
Several other releases, including revised third-quarter gross domestic product, are slated for next week.
